exposure: Mode of birth (cesarean section vs. vaginal delivery)
Maternal knowledge and perception of breastfeeding
outcome: Initiation of breastfeeding within the first hour after delivery
cohort: The study included 1,008 mothers of children aged 6-24 months attending primary healthcare centers for immunizations or routine check-ups in the Aseer region of Saudi Arabia.
finding: This study found a low prevalence of EBF in the Aseer region (13%), with EBF being less frequent among mothers with higher education and those who delivered via cesarean section, but more common among mothers with higher parity, more previous breastfed children, and those without postpartum or infant birth complications.
mod_finding: EBF was less frequent among mothers who delivered via cesarean section (7.9%) compared to those who had a vaginal delivery (15.8%).
